knobs.note: 1 makes the lane decide and log without acting.

Remedy for an item whose board evidence could not be fetched (BH-2548). `escalate-missing` (default) runs bin/responder-fix/escalate-missing.sh: one strict fleet_alert beat per project, no model call. `none` journals and stamps the cooldown only. `model` restores the old path (decision call + tooled call). Any other name runs bin/responder-fix/<name>.sh; a junk value or a name with no file is logged and falls back to `model`.

Remedy for an item whose FETCHED ticket says waitingOn=client and has no open PR matching its key (BH-2548). `none` (default) journals and stamps the 12h cooldown with no model call. `model` restores the old path. Any other name runs bin/responder-fix/<name>.sh; a junk value or a name with no file is logged and falls back to `model`.

0 makes this lane call no model at all. bin/lib/llm-gate.sh refuses BEFORE the vendor call and writes a zero-cost row_source=refused row, so the stop is visible in the ledger rather than being a lane that went quiet.

Comma/space list of the ONLY ladder rungs this lane may reach. Empty is every rung, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. A rung outside the list is refused before the call, so a cliff or a failure on the standing lane cannot descend into one that costs ~100x (#1141, the $793 descent).

Dollars this lane may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend — never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. A second, project-scoped ceiling is the lane.<id>.<project>.llm_usd_cap_day row, which is read only when somebody wrote it.

Dollars this lane may spend in one UTC day, resolved by bin/lib/lane-caps.sh over catalog/lane-caps.conf (now: 150). 0 STOPS the lane; `off` runs it uncapped; nothing is dropped when it trips — the queue waits and it pages once a day. This is the cap BH-1039 added after alert-triage burned $793 in 12 hours inside its session cap. The env suffix is the CAP lane name `responder` from catalog/lane-caps.conf, not this registry id.

Evidence bytes this lane may put in ONE prompt, resolved by bin/lib/lane-caps.sh over catalog/lane-caps.conf (now: 60000). Truncation carries a marker; too small and a family is re-spooled every tick and never triaged, which pages once a day and bills nothing. The env suffix is the CAP lane name `responder` from catalog/lane-caps.conf, not this registry id.

Cumulative context tokens (input + cache_read) ONE session of this lane may reach before bin/agent-call.sh stops it. The evidence cap bounds the prompt; this bounds the session, including everything the tool loop reads. 0 derives the ceiling from the runner's `cliff_tokens` in catalog/model-prices.json instead (CONTEXT_KILL_CLIFF), which on a model with no cliff leaves the lane's 6,000,000 ceiling in catalog/context-budgets.json standing; a positive value is the ceiling verbatim.

How far under the runner's price cliff the derived ceiling sits, when RESPONDER_CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS is 0: the session is stopped at `cliff_tokens - this`. A margin at or past the cliff floors the ceiling at 1000 tokens and says so in logs/failovers.log rather than clamping silently.
